what_its_for: Lindane is used to treat scabies (tiny mites that burrow into your skin and cause intense itching) and lice (tiny insects that live on your scalp, body, or pubic area). It works by killing the parasites and their eggs. Lindane is only used when other safer treatments have not worked or cannot be used.
how_to_take: FOR LOTION (Scabies): Apply a thin layer of lotion to dry skin from your neck down to the soles of your feet. Make sure skin is clean, cool, and dry before applying — do not apply right after a hot bath or shower. Leave the lotion on for 8 to 12 hours, then wash it off completely in the shower or bath. One application is usually enough. FOR SHAMPOO (Lice): Apply the shampoo to dry hair and scalp. Rub it in well and leave it on for exactly 4 minutes — use a timer. Then add a small amount of water and lather, then rinse thoroughly. Use a fine-tooth comb to remove any remaining nits (lice eggs). One application is usually all that is needed. Avoid getting lindane in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If contact occurs, rinse immediately with plenty of water.
dosing: Use lindane ONLY ONCE unless your doctor specifically tells you otherwise. Using it more than directed greatly increases the risk of serious side effects. Adults and children over 110 pounds (50 kg): Apply the full recommended amount as directed. Children and smaller adults: Your doctor will determine a smaller safe amount based on body weight. Children under 2 years old, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers should NOT use lindane — safer alternatives should be used instead.
missed_dose: Lindane is typically used as a single, one-time treatment, so there is no regular dosing schedule. If you forget to wash it off within the recommended time, rinse it off as soon as you remember. Do NOT leave it on longer than directed, as this increases the risk of serious side effects like seizures. Do not apply a second dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
storage: Store lindane at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat and open flame — lindane is flammable. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom where it may get damp. Dispose of any unused lindane properly — ask your pharmacist how to safely throw it away. Never pour it down the drain or toilet.
what_to_avoid: Do not use lindane more than once or in larger amounts than prescribed — this is very dangerous. Do not apply to open wounds, broken skin, or irritated skin, as it will be absorbed too quickly into the bloodstream. Do not apply right after a hot shower or bath — this increases absorption and risk of toxicity. Avoid getting lindane in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Do not use on premature infants. Avoid letting others, especially children, come into contact with treated skin while the medication is on. Do not use if you have a history of seizures. Wash all clothing, bedding, and towels in hot water to prevent reinfestation — but this does NOT require a second dose of lindane.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you or anyone in your household experiences: seizures or convulsions, uncontrollable shaking or tremors, dizziness or loss of balance, confusion or difficulty thinking clearly, severe skin rash, blistering, or burning where the medication was applied, or nausea and vomiting. Also call your doctor if itching does not improve within 4 weeks after treatment (some itching after scabies treatment is normal even when the mites are gone). Call if you accidentally swallowed any lindane — this is a medical emergency. Seek emergency help immediately.
when_it_works: Lindane kills the lice or mites soon after application. However, itching from scabies can continue for 2 to 4 weeks after successful treatment — this is normal and does not mean the treatment failed. For lice, you may see dead lice after treatment, but nits (eggs) may still be visible in the hair — use a fine-tooth comb to remove them. If you still see live lice or new burrows from mites after 1 to 2 weeks, contact your doctor before using lindane again.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do not use lindane. It can be absorbed through the skin and may harm the unborn baby. Ask your doctor for a safer alternative like permethrin. BREASTFEEDING: Do not use lindane. It can pass into breast milk and harm your baby. If treatment is absolutely necessary, pump and discard breast milk for at least 24 hours after use. CHILDREN: Use with extreme caution. Children are at much higher risk for serious side effects including seizures. Children under 2 years old should NOT use lindane. Use the smallest effective amount and apply only once. ELDERLY (over 65): Use with caution. Older adults may absorb more lindane through their skin, increasing the risk of side effects. Discuss safer alternatives with your doctor. SEIZURE DISORDERS: Do not use lindane if you have a history of seizures or epilepsy, as lindane lowers the seizure threshold. HIV/AIDS or IMMUNE DISORDERS: Let your doctor know, as you may have a severe form of scabies (crusted or Norwegian scabies) that requires a different treatment approach.
